slide_text: Agentic Reverse Engineering: From I/O to Code with Discovery Agent

Yihong Dong¹˒², Jiaru Qian³, Haoran Zhang⁴, Peixu Wang⁵, Binhua Li², Zhi Jin³, Yongbin Li², Ge Li³, Xiaokang Yang¹, Xue Jiang²˒³¹ Shanghai Jiao Tong University; ² Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group; ³ Peking University; ⁴ Renmin University of China; ⁵ National University of Singapore
Introduction

• IO2Code infers hidden program rules without explicit natural-language specifications.
◦ Program behavior provides the basis for induction.
◦ Beyond reuse of familiar programming patterns.
• DIO-Agent combines curriculum-based evolutionary search with simplicity-guided mutations.
◦ Discourages memorization of observed behavior.
◦ Avoids structurally complex dead ends.
• IO2CodeBench evaluations support effective, generalizable behavior-driven program discovery.
◦ Discourages memorization and structurally complex dead ends.
• Target applications include reverse engineering, legacy-system migration, and scientific discovery.
Motivation Example

• Prime factorization exposes rule-discovery challenges from input-output observations alone.
• Missing language specifications risk memorization and complex but incorrect programs.
• Increasing expressiveness reveals limitations of successive hypotheses.
◦ Constants → variables → conditionals → iteration
• DIO-Agent structures discovery, discourages overfitting, and uses failures to guide refinement.
Methodology
Curriculum-wise Evolution

• Nested curriculum stages introduce structurally simple examples before expanding behavioral specifications.
• Search islands inherit the preceding stage’s best program, preserving useful discoveries.
• Replay examples retain learned behavior as candidates adapt to new cases.
• Held-out tests assess only the final program, separating search from generalization.
Transformation-priority Guided Mutation

• Mutation favors simple changes; complexity increases only when simpler alternatives cannot explain visible examples.
• Explicit prohibitions reject memorized lookup tables and exact-input matching.
Error-Grounded Feedback

• Output mismatches and runtime errors guide mutations.
◦ Evidence spans curriculum and replay examples.
Experiments
Main Results

• DIO-Agent achieves a 58.63% average score on IO2CodeBench.
• Matches or exceeds strongest baselines across all benchmark levels.
Performance Across Different LLMs

• DIO-Agent improves average discovery performance across all three tested backbones.
◦ DeepSeek V3.2, Qwen-3.6-Plus, Claude-Sonnet-4.6
Ablation Study
• All three specialized components contribute to DIO-Agent’s 58.63% average score.

• Removing transformation-priority guidance lowers performance to 53.80%.
• Removing error-grounded feedback lowers performance to 54.61%.
Comparison with Test-Time Scaling Methods.

• DIO-Agent achieves 63.66%, outperforming Best-of-N at 40.28%.
• Matched sampling budgets of 40 control candidate-generation effort across strategies.
Further Analysis

• Successful discovery correlates with simplification and stable program structure.
◦ Continued complexity growth often accompanies overfitting.
Autonomous Discovery via Active Exploration

• DIO-Agent achieves 60.84% average performance versus AlphaEvolve’s 46.61%.
• Agents construct evidence by selecting inputs and querying a ground-truth oracle.
Conclusion

• IO2Code tests program induction from input-output observations, complementing natural-language code generation.
• IO2CodeBench and DIO-Agent enable benchmarking and structured evolutionary program discovery.
